delivery.safetyIntro: Take it slow. If you feel overwhelmed, stop, open your eyes, move around, or take a break.
delivery.instructions: Send the safety intro before the selected practice. Never describe a practice as medical treatment.

practices.title: Yawn and Stretch
practices.smsText: If it feels comfortable, yawn and gently stretch your arms, shoulders, and neck. Notice what you feel in your body for one minute.

practices.title: Sit and Observe
practices.smsText: Sit somewhere safe and notice the world around you. Name three things you see, two things you hear, and one thing you feel.

practices.title: Mindful Hand Washing
practices.smsText: While washing your hands, slow down. Notice the water, temperature, soap, and movement. Let this bring you back to the present moment.

practices.title: The STOP Method
practices.smsText: Stand up if comfortable. Tune in to your body. Observe one physical sensation. Then picture one helpful next step you could take.

practices.title: Transition Moment
practices.smsText: While moving to your next place—an appointment, meal, job, or visit—slow down. Feel each step and arrive with care.
practices.adaptationNote: Updated the original facility-specific examples for community reentry.

practices.title: Mindful Breathing
practices.smsText: Notice your breathing for one minute without trying to change it. When your mind wanders, gently return to the next breath.

practices.title: Loving Kindness
practices.smsText: Quietly offer yourself this wish: May I be safe. May I have peace. Then offer the same wish to someone else.

practices.title: Set an Intention
practices.smsText: Pause and ask: How do I want to move through today? Choose one simple intention, such as patience, courage, or taking one step at a time.

practices.title: Self-Compassion
practices.smsText: Notice one hard thing without judging yourself. Say: This is hard, and I can be kind to myself while I take the next step.

practices.title: Mindful Hug
practices.smsText: With someone you trust and their clear permission, share a side hug and take three comfortable breaths. Or place a hand on your own shoulder.
practices.adaptationNote: Added explicit consent and a self-directed alternative.

practices.title: Mindful Eating
practices.smsText: For the next minute, slow down while eating. Notice the smell, taste, texture, and each movement before taking another bite.

practices.title: Morning Pause
practices.smsText: Before starting your day, sit or stand comfortably for one minute. Notice your breath and choose one gentle intention for the morning.

practices.title: Seated Pause
practices.smsText: When you sit down, pause for one minute. Feel the seat supporting you, place your feet down if comfortable, and notice your breathing.
practices.adaptationNote: Renamed and adapted the original 'Stool Meditation' for community settings.

practices.title: 4-7-8 Breathing
practices.smsText: Only if holding your breath feels comfortable: breathe in gently for 4, hold for 7, and breathe out for 8. Otherwise, breathe normally and notice one breath.
practices.adaptationNote: Added a comfort-based alternative for text delivery.

practices.title: Box Breathing
practices.smsText: Picture a square. Trace one side as you breathe in, pause at the corner, breathe out along the next side, then pause. Keep every breath comfortable.

practices.title: Door Reset
practices.smsText: As you pass through a doorway, pause. Feel your feet, notice one breath, and enter the next space with a fresh intention.

practices.title: Body Scan
practices.smsText: With your eyes open or closed, slowly notice your jaw, shoulders, hands, and feet. If you find tension, let it soften only as much as feels comfortable.

practices.title: Notice Outside
practices.smsText: If you are somewhere safe, choose a cloud, bird, tree, or another thing around you. Give it your full attention for one minute.
practices.adaptationNote: Broadened the title while preserving the original observation exercise.

practices.title: Mindful Listening
practices.smsText: Listen closely to music or the sounds around you. Notice one sound near you, one farther away, and one you had not noticed before.

practices.title: One Minute of Gratitude
practices.smsText: Name one person, place, or small moment you appreciate today. Notice why it matters to you and stay with that feeling for one minute.

practices.title: One Thing at a Time
practices.smsText: If you are doing several things at once, pause. Choose one small thing and give it your full attention for the next minute.
